To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the entire set (of about 7000) of positive monad bundles is ruled out on the basis of phenomenological considerations, and that there is at least one non-positive monad bundle that gives rise to a standard-like model.
the original data-set of about 70000 models contains 91 models which we describe completely.

(i) the original data set contains 91 standard like models; (ii) none of these gives precisely the standard model matter field content; (iii) we construct a standard model within the class of non-positive two term monads; and (iv) the entire set of two term monads on complete intersections is ruled out on the basis of the phenomenological criterion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic analysis of the entire class of heterotic standard models.
the construction of new supersymmetric models of particle physics based on the heterotic string.
the construction and analysis of new supersymmetric standard-like models within the heterotic string theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entire set (positive and negative) of monads is ruled out on the basis of phenomenology, but there are a number of interesting exceptions.
the class of non-positive two-term monads contains a heterotic standard model but not a standard-like model.
the entire class of monad bundles on complete intersection Calbi-Yau manifold is ruled out on the basis of phenomenological criteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the class of positive two-term heterotic monad bundles on complete intersection Calabis-Yau manifold has been fully analyzed and ruled out on phenomenolgical grounds.
we have found the first supersymmetric standard model with no exotics and no extra vector-like matter in the heterotic string.

, although we have ruled out the entire class of positive monad bundles on complete intersection Calabis-Yau manifols, we have also constructed an example of a non-positive monad bundle that gives rise to a supersymmetric heteroti standard model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of any further constraints, there are no restrictions on the allowed gauge groups, chiral spectra and Yukawa couplings for supersymmetric heterotic models based on non-positive monad bundles on complete intersection Calabis-Yau threefolding.

, in the heterotic string landscape, the class of monad bundles is not ruled out on theoretical or phenomenological grounds, but rather that it has not yet been explored to the extent that one might have thought.
there is a rich variety of heterotic standard models, some of them quite different from the standard model of particle physics.
